endorsements.quote: Professional accountability and ethical responsibility toward patients must unequivocally remain with human practitioners and educators.

Recognizing that clinical educators themselves frequently lack digital proficiency, institutions must mandate faculty empowerment programs alongside training students in algorithmic logic, data privacy, and critical appraisal.

Furthermore, trainees must be guided to evaluate AI outputs against regional epidemiological realities while remaining critically aware of the structural limitations and hidden flaws inherent in local healthcare data sets [ 10 ].
Ultimately, AI agents must be integrated strictly as cognitive scaffolds that support human expertise rather than systems that replace the cognitive processes required for clinical excellence.

unlisted_practices: Incorporate AI-supported virtual patient simulations that expose learners to diagnostic uncertainty and AI limitations in medical training.
Design AI agents as cognitive partners that prompt learners to articulate decision rationale and evaluate alternative interpretations.
Evolve clinical assessments to evaluate learners' ability to critically interpret, validate, and integrate AI-generated information.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/commentary article discussing the opportunities, challenges, and governance recommendations for integrating AI agents into medical education and clinical judgment training.
